# FDG9143

> DO use `ReadOnlyMemory<T>` in place of `ReadOnlySpan<T>` in asynchronous methods.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.12 Operating on Buffers.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9143
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Use ReadOnlyMemory<{0}> instead of ReadOnlySpan<{0}> for the parameter '{1}' of the asynchronous method '{2}'

The text has no body; the body of FDG9144 gives the reason for both. FDG9143 reports a ReadOnlySpan<T> parameter of a method, of any accessibility, that returns a task-like type (as for FDG9020) or IAsyncEnumerable<T>. An async method cannot declare such a parameter (CS4012 in a probe with SDK 10.0.402), so the reports are on methods that return a task without the async keyword. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported, since their parameter types come from another member, and local functions, lambdas and delegate types are not checked, so coverage is partial. Span<T> and Memory<T> types need .NET Core 2.1 or later, or the System.Memory package on .NET Framework and .NET Standard 2.0 (see FDG9137). Changing the parameter type changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.
